question: According to Einstein's equation, the photoelectric effect obeys the law of conservation of energy. If the intensity of the incident light is doubled while keeping the frequency constant, why does the maximum kinetic energy ($K_{max}$) of the photoelectrons remain unchanged?

options.A: Because increasing intensity splits the photon energy into smaller packets
options.B: Because the energy of an individual photon depends only on frequency, not the total number of photons
options.C: Because the work function of the metal increases with intensity
options.D: Because the extra energy is absorbed by the nucleus
